title: A Tumblr thematic analysis of perinatal health: Where users go to seek support
screen_reason: Thematic analysis of 235 Tumblr text posts on perinatal/women's health collected over four days; seven posts were flagged as misinformation, reported as a share of the whole corpus ('accounted for only 3% of the total sample of posts (7/235)'). That is a CONTENT share with a denominator, even though the paper's aim is thematic/sentiment description.

estimates.country: Not reported (Tumblr does not require users to give a location; non-English posts were removed; authors based in Canada)
estimates.measure_type: % of perinatal/women's-health Tumblr posts flagged as misinformation
estimates.value_raw: 7/235 ('accounted for only 3% of the total sample of posts (7/235)')
estimates.denominator: 235 English-language Tumblr text posts retained after cleaning (from 676 collected via the Tumblr API on 43 perinatal/women's-health keywords; removals: 244 non-text, 80 duplicates, 15 near-duplicates, 9 non-English, 93 irrelevant)
estimates.definition: Posts flagged as 'misinformation' by the two coders because of their content, e.g. posts suggesting non-evidence-based treatments and natural remedies (essential oils for labour, herbs/natural vitamins for menopausal or pregnancy symptoms) without sufficient scientific evidence; they sit inside a combined 'Misinformation/advertisement' category of 30 posts, of which the other 23 are advertisements
estimates.misinfo_def: Misinformation refers to information that is false and is being shared by an individual who thinks it is true, whereas disinformation refers to someone knowingly sharing false information
estimates.source_quote: Misinformation, although present on the platform, accounted for only 3% of the total sample of posts (7/235).
estimates.page_loc: Discussion section 5, p. 8; also Results section 4.1.6 'Misinformation/advertisement' and Abstract
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Both co-first authors independently coded/reviewed the dataset and the thematic categories; disagreements resolved by consensus with the third author reviewing; no formal reliability statistic (kappa) reported and no external ground truth beyond 'sufficient scientific evidence'.
estimates.moderator_quote: Of the 30 posts, 7 were flagged as 'misinformation' due to the content of the post. For example, posts suggested nonevidence-based treatment and natural remedies to get pregnant ... The remaining 16 posts were advertisements for gynecologist and obstetric doctors in specific regions.
estimates.notes: 7/235 = 2.98%, reported by the authors as 3%; the verbatim 3% is kept. The 30-post category is 'Misinformation and ads' but the 7 misinformation posts are separately identified, so the misinformation numerator is clean. Keyword corpus is one topical domain (perinatal/women's health, 43 keywords), hence denom_scope=topical with no curation: the API returned the posts made in a 4-day window rather than a top-N list. Coding is by two health-science researchers against 'sufficient scientific evidence', not against a formal ground truth, so confidence medium. The quotes printed in the paper are stated to be re-written representative posts (for anonymity), which does not affect the counts.

missed_or_uncertain: Not extracted: the 14% (33/235) 'awareness and education' share and the other thematic category counts (not misinformation); the VADER sentiment scores (means, not shares). The 30-post 'Misinformation and ads' category as a whole (12.8%) was not coded as a misinformation share because 23 of the 30 are advertisements.

rob.design: Netnographic content analysis of a 4-day Tumblr API capture (18-21 Aug 2023) on 43 perinatal/women's-health keywords; 676 posts collected, 235 retained after a documented 5-step cleaning pipeline; inductive thematic analysis by two independent coders with consensus resolution plus VADER sentiment scoring; no reliability coefficient reported; user location unavailable.
rob.item6_quote: Misinformation refers to information that is false and is being shared by an individual who thinks it is true, whereas disinformation refers to someone knowingly sharing false information
rob.item10_quote: Misinformation, although present on the platform, accounted for only 3% of the total sample of posts (7/235).
